data.title: Will Bonterra Resources (CVE:BTR) Spend Its Cash Wisely?
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. Having said that, unprofitable companies are risky because they could potentially burn through all their cash and become distressed.

So should Bonterra Resources (CVE:BTR) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? In this report, we will consider the company's annual negative free cash flow, henceforth referring to it as the 'cash burn'. First, we'll determine its cash runway by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

When Might Bonterra Resources Run Out Of Money?

A company's cash runway is the amount of time it would take to burn through its cash reserves at its current cash burn rate. As at September 2026, Bonterra Resources had cash of CA$15m and no debt. Looking at the last year, the company burnt through CA$13m. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. While that cash runway isn't too concerning, sensible holders would be peering into the distance, and considering what happens if the company runs out of cash. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

View our latest analysis for Bonterra Resources

How Is Bonterra Resources' Cash Burn Changing Over Time?

Because Bonterra Resources isn't currently generating revenue, we consider it an early-stage business. So while we can't look to sales to understand growth, we can look at how the cash burn is changing to understand how expenditure is trending over time. Over the last year its cash burn actually increased by a very significant 89%. While this spending increase is no doubt intended to drive growth, if the trend continues the company's cash runway will shrink very quickly. Bonterra Resources makes us a little nervous due to its lack of substantial operating revenue. We prefer most of the stocks on this list of stocks that analysts expect to grow.

Can Bonterra Resources Raise More Cash Easily?

While Bonterra Resources does have a solid cash runway, its cash burn trajectory may have some shareholders thinking ahead to when the company may need to raise more cash. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Bonterra Resources has a market capitalisation of CA$46m and burnt through CA$13m last year, which is 28% of the company's market value. That's fairly notable cash burn, so if the company had to sell shares to cover the cost of another year's operations, shareholders would suffer some costly dilution.

Is Bonterra Resources' Cash Burn A Worry?

Even though its increasing cash burn makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Bonterra Resources' cash runway was relatively promising. Summing up, we think the Bonterra Resources' cash burn is a risk, based on the factors we mentioned in this article. data.title: What Investors Got Wrong About Applied Digital Before The Drop
data.description:
A year that featured Applied Digital signing a 15-year AI lease that pushed contracted revenue above US$23b, spinning off ChronoScale, and lining up huge power deals sounds like the kind of story long term holders hope for. Holding Applied Digital over the past year would have meant a 45.5% loss, including dividends. If you had bought on 20 November 2025, how much of that outcome was already hinted at in the early bull and bear cases?

A Narrative on Simply Wall St is one investor's written case for a company, with its growth, margin and multiple assumptions spelled out. Those assumptions imply an estimated Fair Value.

Applied Digital is not the only name tied to this theme. Zero in on 53 AI infrastructure stocks and compare how each one is priced.

The Two Applied Digital Stories Investors Had To Weigh

The shares cost US$21.37 at the start, and anyone looking at Applied Digital then was really choosing between two tight but very different stories.

The bullish narrative saw Fair Value at US$24, or 12% above the start price. That view leaned on assumed revenue growth of 82.0% a year over three years and profit margins shifting from heavy losses to 28.7%, supported by long AI leases.

The bearish case put Fair Value at US$13, or 39% below the start price. It accepted fast 75.4% revenue growth assumptions but focused on high debt and the risk that tighter regulation and supply chain problems would squeeze margins to just 2.6% and justify a 273.2x future P/E.

What The Evidence Did To The Applied Digital Story

Applied Digital signed several 15 year AI leases worth tens of billions of US dollars in contracted revenue, which directly backed the bullish focus on long contracts and hyperscaler demand. The measured results told a different story on profitability. Revenue reached US$341.9m in Q1 2027, while the business still reported a loss and net margin fell to -64.7%. The period cut both ways.

The whole episode turned on one assumption. You can accept aggressive growth forecasts only if you also track whether profit and net margin are actually moving toward the promised target, quarter by quarter, not just whether big contracts are announced.

What You Are Paying For In Applied Digital Today

Applied Digital trades at US$11.49 today after a 45.5% loss over the past year, and the bearish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St places its Fair Value above that level based on contracted AI and HPC growth.

The same Narrative argues that for the higher figure to hold, new AI and power projects would need funding on terms that keep interest costs from overwhelming future earnings.

"Although Applied Digital highlights roughly $36 billion of contracted revenue across long term leases, the recent net loss of about $221 million from continuing operations in fiscal Q1 2027, driven by very high SG&A and noncash warrant losses, signals that scaling into this contract base could still leave the company struggling to translate future revenue into sustained earnings and cash flow."

That disagreement has a full argument behind it. → Uncover the higher Fair Value this Narrative argues for

Where Applied Digital’s Theme Extends

Applied Digital leans on huge AI workloads. Those workloads still need somewhere to run.

One large software and cloud provider is racing to host more of that demand. It sells access through subscriptions and usage based services.

The same customers pushing AI at Applied Digital often want integrated tools. This other business bundles office software, developer tools and agents around its cloud.

As AI projects expand, your question becomes sharper. Does value sit mostly in specialized infrastructure, or in platforms that tie AI, data and everyday software together?

data.title: Insiders At Pacific Biosciences of California Sold US$1.3m In Stock, Alluding To Potential Weakness
data.description:
In the last year, many Pacific Biosciences of California, Inc. (NASDAQ:PACB) insiders sold a substantial stake in the company which may have sparked shareholders' attention. When evaluating insider transactions, knowing whether insiders are buying is usually more beneficial than knowing whether they are selling, as the latter can be open to many interpretations. However, when multiple insiders sell stock over a specific duration, shareholders should take notice as that could possibly be a red flag.

While we would never suggest that investors should base their decisions solely on what the directors of a company have been doing, we do think it is perfectly logical to keep tabs on what insiders are doing.

We've found 21 US stocks that are forecast to pay a dividend yield of over 6% next year. See the full list for free.

The Last 12 Months Of Insider Transactions At Pacific Biosciences of California

The Senior Business Advisor & Director, Christian O. Henry, made the biggest insider sale in the last 12 months. That single transaction was for US$752k worth of shares at a price of US$1.63 each. So it's clear an insider wanted to take some cash off the table, even slightly below the current price of US$1.63. We generally consider it a negative if insiders have been selling, especially if they did so below the current price, because it implies that they considered a lower price to be reasonable. Please do note, however, that sellers may have a variety of reasons for selling, so we don't know for sure what they think of the stock price. This single sale was just 28% of Christian O. Henry's stake.

In the last year Pacific Biosciences of California insiders didn't buy any company stock. The chart below shows insider transactions (by companies and individuals) over the last year. If you click on the chart, you can see all the individual transactions, including the share price, individual, and the date!

See our latest analysis for Pacific Biosciences of California

If you like to buy stocks that insiders are buying, rather than selling, then you might just love this free list of companies. (Hint: Most of them are flying under the radar).

Pacific Biosciences of California Insiders Are Selling The Stock

Over the last three months, we've seen a bit of insider selling at Pacific Biosciences of California. insider Kathy Ordonez only netted US$33k selling shares, in that period. It's not great to see insider selling, nor the lack of recent buyers. But the volume sold is so low that it really doesn't bother us.

Insider Ownership Of Pacific Biosciences of California

Many investors like to check how much of a company is owned by insiders. Usually, the higher the insider ownership, the more likely it is that insiders will be incentivised to build the company for the long term. Our data indicates that Pacific Biosciences of California insiders own about US$5.2m worth of shares (which is 1.0% of the company). Overall, this level of ownership isn't that impressive, but it's certainly better than nothing!

So What Does This Data Suggest About Pacific Biosciences of California Insiders?

While there has not been any insider buying in the last three months, there has been selling. But the sales were small, so we're not concerned. Recent insider selling makes us a little nervous, in light of the broader picture of Pacific Biosciences of California insider transactions. And usually insiders own more stock in the company, according to our data. So while it's helpful to know what insiders are doing in terms of buying or selling, it's also helpful to know the risks that a particular company is facing. data.title: We Think Pioneer Power Solutions (NASDAQ:PPSI) Needs To Drive Business Growth Carefully
data.description:
We can readily understand why investors are attracted to unprofitable companies. For example, although Amazon.com made losses for many years after listing, if you had bought and held the shares since 1999, you would have made a fortune. But while history lauds those rare successes, those that fail are often forgotten; who remembers Pets.com?

So should Pioneer Power Solutions (NASDAQ:PPSI) shareholders be worried about its cash burn? For the purpose of this article, we'll define cash burn as the amount of cash the company is spending each year to fund its growth (also called its negative free cash flow). We'll start by comparing its cash burn with its cash reserves in order to calculate its cash runway.

This technology could replace computers: discover the 20 stocks are working to make quantum computing a reality.

When Might Pioneer Power Solutions Run Out Of Money?

A cash runway is defined as the length of time it would take a company to run out of money if it kept spending at its current rate of cash burn. As at September 2026, Pioneer Power Solutions had cash of US$9.4m and no debt. Importantly, its cash burn was US$8.1m over the trailing twelve months. So it had a cash runway of approximately 14 months from September 2026. That's not too bad, but it's fair to say the end of the cash runway is in sight, unless cash burn reduces drastically. The image below shows how its cash balance has been changing over the last few years.

Check out our latest analysis for Pioneer Power Solutions

How Well Is Pioneer Power Solutions Growing?

We reckon the fact that Pioneer Power Solutions managed to shrink its cash burn by 26% over the last year is rather encouraging. Unfortunately, however, operating revenue declined by 37% during the period. In light of the data above, we're fairly sanguine about the business growth trajectory. Clearly, however, the crucial factor is whether the company will grow its business going forward. So you might want to take a peek at how much the company is expected to grow in the next few years.

Can Pioneer Power Solutions Raise More Cash Easily?

Pioneer Power Solutions seems to be in a fairly good position, in terms of cash burn, but we still think it's worthwhile considering how easily it could raise more money if it wanted to. Issuing new shares, or taking on debt, are the most common ways for a listed company to raise more money for its business. Many companies end up issuing new shares to fund future growth. We can compare a company's cash burn to its market capitalisation to get a sense for how many new shares a company would have to issue to fund one year's operations.

Pioneer Power Solutions has a market capitalisation of US$23m and burnt through US$8.1m last year, which is 35% of the company's market value. That's not insignificant, and if the company had to sell enough shares to fund another year's growth at the current share price, you'd likely witness fairly costly dilution.

Is Pioneer Power Solutions' Cash Burn A Worry?

Even though its falling revenue makes us a little nervous, we are compelled to mention that we thought Pioneer Power Solutions' cash burn reduction was relatively promising. Looking at the factors mentioned in this short report, we do think that its cash burn is a bit risky, and it does make us slightly nervous about the stock.
